source_note: First source a paid artefact or offer. M2 means seller's price, NOT buyer paid proof. Supplementary source is competitor/verification pass, not new attempt. All buyer cases distinct from IDs 761–777. No outreach.

cases.spend_capture_test: The payer purchases electrical design and reliable manufacturability, not mere Gerber exports
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: Circuit brief/component choices -> verified schematics, nets, Gerbers and fabrication-ready BOM
cases.verification_oracle: ERC/DRC checks exist but cannot validate electrical intent of unbuilt prototype
cases.AI_repeated: LLM can sketch schematics but repeated correct engineering and power/EMC verification need expert
cases.AI_built: EDA automation easy to copy; each hardware design requires engineering review
cases.first_ten_access: UK hardware design founder directories, ten matching buyers not verified
cases.second_kill: True electrical judgement and component availability define purchased result; ongoing expert liability
cases.next_attack: Do not build; separate deterministic CAD DRC is included by EDA

cases.payer: UK architect or building surveyor with registered point cloud
cases.price: indicative £3–£10 per m²; separate point-cloud-only and modelling tiers
cases.spend_capture_test: Model-only outcome independently quoted; physical survey avoided; no documented buyer switching away from established Revit firms
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: Supplied registered E57/RCP cloud -> LOD-defined Revit/IFC model and measured deviation report
cases.verification_oracle: Compare point cloud/model deviation within job-specified tolerances; cannot automatically verify occluded dimensions/family semantics
cases.AI_repeated: AI image segmentation improves starting geometry; human Revit model QA remains
cases.AI_built: AI-assisted geometry-to-Revit workflows exist; maintaining Revit/IFC accuracy and support costly
cases.first_ten_access: RICS surveyors and architect firms; no verified first ten with absent incumbent solution
cases.second_kill: No demonstrated unattended complete Revit model at professional accuracy, multiple mature service providers; too much manual QA
cases.next_attack: Independent sample dataset + acceptance diff; reject if required manual specialist review per project

cases.trigger: new customer sketch must become production cut file
cases.spend_capture_test: A real separate digital production service, but exact CAD designers already sell cheap output
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: Dimensioned sketch/PDF -> clean dimensioned DXF layers/no open contours
cases.verification_oracle: CAD entity topological checks; dimensions/reference lengths need human source validation
cases.AI_repeated: AI/tracing can handle simple outlines repeatedly but machine-relevant tolerances ambiguous
cases.AI_built: Batch vectorisation and contour validation straightforward, competing utility already cheap
cases.first_ten_access: UK laser-cutting fab directories, ten named user buyers not verified
cases.second_kill: Outsourced price £45 includes human interpretation of dimensions; narrow deterministic checks unlikely to justify separate subscription

cases.payer: UK ecommerce product brand with 3D CAD
cases.trigger: SKU launch requiring listing-ready consistent images
cases.price: from £90 per SKU; modelling separately from £150/model
cases.spend_capture_test: Standalone render deliverable sold independently but supplier requires approved 3D model and human reference image sign-off
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: STEP/OBJ/3D geometry+materials -> approval-matched view/variant PNG render set
cases.verification_oracle: Pixel/resolution/file checks machine-verifiable, look/geometry truth not fully verifiable without designer
cases.AI_repeated: Generative AI can produce rough visuals but often violates exact geometry; traditional rendering needs template setup
cases.AI_built: Ready-made rendering tools and full-service vendors own workflow
cases.first_ten_access: UK ecommerce product brands; no ten buyer-selection proofs
cases.second_kill: Human material/camera QA and cheap local automation make a separate generic rendering SaaS weak

cases.payer: UK/Irish recruiting agency managing live vacancies
cases.paid_outcome: outsourced candidate research, contact and ATS updates
cases.spend_capture_test: Retainer buys staff availability, LinkedIn/job-board access, candidate replies and qualified engagement not only list research
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: Vacancy brief -> qualified responsive candidates and accurate ATS status
cases.verification_oracle: Candidate intent and suitability are subjective and depend on platform permission
cases.AI_repeated: AI can draft outreach and mine public profiles but cannot repeatedly access/respond legally or secure candidate interest
cases.AI_built: An AI sourcing bot remains partial; platform/licensing and privacy burden heavy
cases.first_ten_access: Agencies UK/IE 2–30 recruiters identifiable, ten not verified
cases.second_kill: Underpriced hours vs human engagement; automated shortlist not complete job

cases.payer: UK knitwear designer placing Shima Seiki manufacturing order
cases.spend_capture_test: File is independently sold, but production-specific knit-machine QA and gauge matter
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: Artwork + machine gauge + stitch spec -> APEX-compatible knitting file with approved test swatch
cases.verification_oracle: Shima APEX includes automatic jacquard conversion, gauge is algorithmic; physical knit proof still needed
cases.AI_repeated: AI/pixel conversion handles standard jacquard repeats; real manufacturing approval needs expert or factory
cases.AI_built: Vendor's own design system already offers native conversion; independent clone has no structural opening
cases.first_ten_access: Knitwear designer/manufacturer registers; ten first buyers unverified
cases.second_kill: Manufacturer-owned conversion and machine validation kill separate incremental paid software
cases.next_attack: No revival without customer-paid exception current APEX cannot solve

cases.payer: UK exhibitor producing booth screen loop
cases.trigger: exhibition approaching needs silent-readable animated display
cases.spend_capture_test: Digital output is separately commissioned but purchased outcome is messaging, creativity, scripting, unlimited revision rather than an accepted deterministic transformation
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: Marketing brief and brand files -> final approved loop at exhibit screen resolutions
cases.verification_oracle: Output video codec measurable, effectiveness and visual messaging subjective
cases.AI_repeated: Repeat general AI can create acceptable low-end clips with human editorial direction
cases.AI_built: AI video assembly accessible; competitive studios own client revisions, no independent structural edge
cases.first_ten_access: UK exhibitor directories accessible; no verified buyer dissatisfaction
cases.second_kill: Price premium buys taste and messaging craft; software delivers only base content

cases.payer: UK sales operations migrating to HubSpot
cases.trigger: switch from legacy CRM threatens relationship histories
cases.spend_capture_test: Clearly independently priced migration service, but complete data integrity includes bespoke fields/history, access and zero downtime
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: Authorized CRM data/assets -> reconciled HubSpot objects, associations, histories and safe go-live
cases.verification_oracle: Record counts and relationship keys checkable; semantics, permissions and custom business mapping need human validation
cases.AI_repeated: AI maps simple CSV schemas and identifies duplicate contacts, fails bespoke cross-system logic at scale
cases.AI_built: HubSpot already supports imports, dedupe, and integrations; independent entrant inherits data/security/migration liability
cases.first_ten_access: HubSpot partners can identify buyers, but migration projects 60–90+ days / no first-ten quick route
cases.second_kill: Very high human onboarding, credentials, failure liability, and adequate partner ecosystem
cases.next_attack: Do not rebrand migration wizard as £5k service

cases.payer: UK architect requiring licensed base maps for planning
cases.trigger: new design site needs georeferenced OS layers
cases.paid_outcome: licensed OS MasterMap CAD digital export
cases.spend_capture_test: The customer pays access to protected Ordnance Survey licensed data; transformation is already self-service
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: Site polygon/location -> official licensed georeferenced DWG/DXF layers
cases.verification_oracle: OSGB36 coordinate and layer format validation possible; intellectual-property licence is authority
cases.AI_repeated: General AI cannot confer data rights; file conversion is trivial
cases.AI_built: Existing license-holder provides self-service complete job; licensing dominates costs
cases.first_ten_access: Architects reachable but no entry rights or repeat buyer channel proven
cases.second_kill: Protected OS data licence, low unit fee, exact incumbent C4

cases.trigger: wedding date approaching; guests need details and RSVPs
cases.spend_capture_test: Digitally delivered site purchased independently; premium is bespoke matching stationery/brand and designer revision
cases.inputs_and_accepted_output: Couple details/guest RSVP fields -> hosted website accepted by couple and usable by guests
cases.verification_oracle: Technical site/RSVP checks easy, bespoke look/guest delight subjective
cases.AI_repeated: AI site builders and free template-based guest/RSVP service solve common cases
cases.AI_built: Free Hitched.ie already delivers entire functional result; paid segment buys design services, not software
cases.first_ten_access: Irish wedding supplier directories reachable but one-time high-CAC acquisition
cases.second_kill: €390 cannot be captured by merely offering functional RSVPs already free
cases.next_attack: Do not revive generic wedding-website builder
